newsitem.title: UK: Major says Britain must take part in EMU debate.
newsitem.headline: Major says Britain must take part in EMU debate.

text.p: Prime Minister John Major on Wednesday said he would not "play partisan politics" by ruling out British membership of a single European currency, saying he had to put the interests of country ahead of party.

Major, under pressure from right-wing elements in his ruling Conservative party to state Britain would never sign up to European Monetary Union (EMU), said a single currency would affect the country whether it was a member or not.

"And that is why as prime minister, with the interests of the British nation as a whole at stake, I am not prepared to play partisan politics. I must be there to represent the British interest," he told BBC radio.

The Conservatives are trailing far behind the opposition Labour party ahead of a May 1 general election. Labour leader Tony Blair said on Tuesday that if he won power, Britain would only join the single currency if the conditions were right.

Britain says it is highly unlikely it will sign up to the first stage of EMU, due to be introduced on January 1 1999, but has vowed to take part in talks on bringing in the so-called Euro single currency.
"As prime minister I need to be in the negotiations right up to last minute for a single currency...since it will have an impact in this country," Major said.

"Let us suppose the other nations went ahead with the European currency on a weak basis and produced a weak Euro. What would happen is that all the money that flows into Europe would flow into the two strong currencies, let us say the Swiss franc and sterling," he said.

"That would put up the exchange rate of sterling, damage our exports and cost us jobs. That is a matter of very direct relevance to us, whether we are in a single currency or whether we are not in a single currency."

Since winning the last election in 1992 Major has had to deal with sustained protests from so-called "Eurosceptics" within his party who fear that Britain would become a slave to its European partners if it signed up to a single currency.
